title: Check: Structure of the Periodic Table

questions.stem: Why do elements in the same group have similar chemical properties?

options.text: They have the same number of electron shells
They have the same number of electrons in their outer shell
They have the same atomic mass
They were discovered at the same time

questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of outer shell electrons. Since chemical reactions involve outer shell electrons, having the same number of outer electrons means they react in similar ways. For example, all Group 1 elements have 1 outer electron and form +1 ions.

questions.stem: In the periodic table, what does the period number tell you about an element?

options.text: The number of outer shell electrons

questions.explanation: The period number tells you how many electron shells an element has. For example, elements in Period 3 (Na to Ar) all have 3 electron shells. The group number, by contrast, tells you the number of outer shell electrons.
